scope_note: SGA1 XIII5.3.0 supplies the strict-local normal-crossing Kummer calculation; SGA7 I provides the tame-inertia action. The finite-level Cech identification is independently checked in reviews/29a/independent_checks.md §7. The precise semiglobal formal-cover category and sign convention are not identified merely by these later references. This is an established local construction, with those reconstruction limits.

The cyclotomic action is explicit in SGA7 I§1. The finite example satisfies ramification index3 prime to residue characteristic2 and residue degree2. It refutes arithmetic centrality without trivializing the action, not a geometric centrality statement.

Let E/C be elliptic, L=O_E(0), M=L^n, n>1. The identity M^n=[n]^*L gives a connected finite tame cover M^×→L^× with central deck extension 1→mu_n→H→E[n]→1 and nondegenerate theta commutator. Completing along zero sections preserves this cover. A split extension with abelian base group and trivial cyclotomic action would have only abelian quotients, contradiction. Mumford1966 §1 Theorem1 and the symmetric pullback formula give the precise primary inputs. The later actual leaf, unlike the earlier note alone, explicitly asserts triviality after excluding P1; no scan reading is changed.

The normal-crossing tame computation and finite Kummer classes fit SGA1 XIII5.3.0. The zero-degree exception follows directly from the displayed cokernel. The notation mu_n requires scan verification if no nonzero-degree hypothesis is present.

Schmidt2007 Theorem6.2 gives a pro-p K(pi,1) after suitable enlargement of S under its stated hypotheses; it does not calculate the full tame pi_2 for every original S. Schmidt2000 treats tame abelian finiteness and normal-crossing local models. The exact all-prime question, with the page's incomplete conventions, is not settled by either source; the residual formulation must be fixed before claiming modern openness.

The polynomial x^3−4x+1 has totally real S3 splitting field and squarefree discriminant229, hence only tame finite ramification. It excludes a universal abelian interpretation even with real places unramified. No general finiteness claim follows from this example, and no uncertain word is selected. Searches through arithmetic tame/K(pi,1) literature did not identify the precise handwritten quantifier.

SGA1 XIII5.3.0 gives the strict-local Kummer theorem and Schmidt2000 §1.2 restates it. This establishes the local input. Pairwise commutation of branch factors is weaker than centrality in the arithmetic group. The semiglobal gluing step must retain its chosen category and cannot be inferred solely from the local theorem.

The finite Kummer and classifying-topos mechanisms were developed in SGA1/SGA4, but no theorem for every formal scheme or ringed topos with these unspecified hypotheses is asserted. The two normal cyclic subgroups of Q8 supply an independent logical counterexample to normality implying commutation.

The eigenvalue-permutation proof is valid and independently re-proved here. SGA7 I1.1 presents the arithmetic quasi-unipotence application and cites the Serre–Tate Appendix for its proof. The source's draft lemma6.5 is not final SGA7 I6.5, which concerns abelian reduction.

The long exact sequence proves left exactness; the small-category category-of-elements argument proves prorepresentability, and Bourbaki Exposé195 A§3 Proposition3.1 and its corollary give strictness for Artinian objects. SGA4 I8.13.3 is a different accessible-category criterion, requiring filtered colimits and other hypotheses; it is not directly applicable to FinAb. SGA4 I8.3.3 is the relevant small-category criterion. Artin–Mazur provides an étale homotopy framework, but that does not identify every unrestricted site-level construction without hypotheses.

SGA1 XIII5.3.0 gives the Kummer local model from which the valuation map follows. The source witnesses do not agree on all arrows and coefficient identifications; this match proves the local calculation, not an unqualified global functorial isomorphism.

The arithmetic criterion is the local Kummer calculation applied prime by prime; it also follows immediately from the adjugate formula and reduction modulo a prime divisor. A rectangular matrix needs separate rank and Smith-normal-form conditions.

Milne Algebraic Groups2017 Proposition11.3 gives exactly G≅G0⋊pi0(G) over a perfect field and identifies G_red with pi0(G). Examples11.4–11.5 show failure over imperfect fields. This standard structure is used by the subsequent finite-torsor theory; it does not assert a splitting over arbitrary bases.

The finite torsor theory is established in Nori's framework with its hypotheses. On Spec k[epsilon]/epsilon², the alpha_p sections0 and epsilon have the same geometric values but are distinct. This directly isolates the failure when reducedness is dropped. It is not a claim that all morphisms between arbitrary pointed S-schemes are rigid.

Nori1976 constructs the pointed fundamental group scheme in its reduced connected proper setting, and Nori1982 develops the theory further. The manuscript's unrestricted variable-base generalization is false without closure/flatness hypotheses; Antei2015 explains why the category of all finite flat S-groups need not have the fibre products used. The constant-field-group category must not be conflated with the larger S-group category.

Zhang2013 Theorem2.1 supplies an exact criterion under reduced connected locally noetherian perfect-field hypotheses, with irreducible base: every G-saturated torsor must satisfy base change for its pushed-forward algebra and the relevant fibre-group image must be normal. Base change alone is insufficient. This is a precise conditional theorem, not blanket exactness for every proper separable morphism.

SGA1 X2.5, originalp271/reprintp208 footnote2, explicitly records an unpublished Artin counterexample already for curves of genus at least2. The exact footnote was visually checked in this run. Pauly2007 supplies a related base-field-extension failure for Nori groups of an ordinary genus2 curve in characteristic2; that later example should not be substituted for the unpublished Artin example.

Mehta–Subramanian2002 is the proper full Nori Kunneth theorem (Theorem2.3 as quoted and used by Zhang). Its publisher page was opened but the paywalled proof was not read. Zhang Corollary3.2 proves the local quotient version; §4 refutes the general nonproper version using A1 and a supersingular elliptic curve. These scopes are kept distinct.

Nori1983, opening theorem, explicitly shows that a pointed finite G-torsor is induced from A[n] for some n, over any field. The first-page theorem was opened in primary OCR. The inverse/direct-limit variance and dual variety are essential; this record does not claim the entire paper's proof was independently rechecked.

Modern Dieudonne theory is a relevant comparator, but the page does not specify the module category, variance, operators or exact family assertion. Searches through Nori, the Grothendieck–Serre correspondence discussion and finite-group literature did not identify one theorem with these quantifiers. The strong family hope is separately refuted in CL-SA12-217; this sketch is not declared a surviving open problem.

Any map from an infinitesimal S-group to a finite etale S-group lands in the identity section by its clopen inverse image containing every geometric point. Applying this in both directions proves uniqueness. Reducedness of S is unnecessary for this step; it belongs to later rigidity arguments. The connected/etale framework is present in SGA3 and Nori.

Fpqc descent of affine schemes and group morphisms supplies the corrected mechanism; SGA1 VIII and SGA3 VIII are exact formalism comparators. The deletion is not attributed to a specific mathematical objection beyond what the page states.

Antei2015 §2 explains the absence of fibre products in the unrestricted finite-flat category. The explicit equalizer A[T]/(T^p,tT) proves the relevant obstruction. It does not refute a manuscript axiom that expressly restricts to categories closed under those kernels.

On the reduced cusp S=Spec k[w^p,w^{p+1}], the nontrivial pointed alpha_p torsor z^p=x is minimal, while0 and[x] have pointed-trivial pushforwards. Their coincidence reduction is the nonflat normalization. Every stated hypothesis of this unrestricted version is checked in §4. The morphism[x] varies with the base, so the example does not lie in the constant k-group morphism category.

The forward statement is the Chinese remainder theorem, verified in Stacks00DT Lemma10.15.4. Ideals(x),(y) in k[x,y] give equality(xy) but sum(x,y)≠1. Scan108 may presuppose extra monic-factor hypotheses; the bare converse is what fails.

CRT and finite-projective module theory give a complete proof: the two quotient factors have constant ranks, characteristic polynomials of multiplication by T generate the two ideals, and block determinants multiply to P. Stacks00DT and00NV verify the two standard inputs. This does not claim an exact historical printing of the fragment was located.

SGA3 XI3.1 and3.5 give precise open-immersion and gluing representability criteria, including fpqc sheaf, filtered-limit and adic-effectivity conditions plus infinitesimal etaleness. They demonstrate which omitted hypotheses matter, but are not an exact match to every draft condition on scan133. Testing only separable extensions cannot replace algebraically closed field tests without further assumptions.

SGA3 XI3.5 explicitly constructs the scheme by gluing open representable subfunctors. Compatibility only over local schemes is insufficient: the local data in §6 would give image{generic point,c}⊂A1, which is not open. The source's inserted neighborhood condition is therefore substantive.

Nori and later relative fundamental-group-scheme work develop such torsor functors under controlled bases; Antei2015 shows why all finite flat S-groups are not automatically a valid filtered system. SGA3 XI3.12 is representability for multiplicative-type Hom/subgroup functors, not a theorem about this arbitrary pointed-torsor functor. The exact scan131 formulation remains unmatched.

The wording and inserted condition match SGA3 VIII Corollary3.4. Under character duality u:N→M, kernel corresponds to coker(u), quotient to im(u), and the closed immersion follows from the character quotient. The finite-type insertion is retained.
Exact match SGA3 VIII3.2–3.3; the group-algebra basis of coset representatives proves faithful flatness. Empty S is excluded only for converse deductions about the underlying abstract groups.
Matched to SGA3 VIII3.5 and§4, with the finite-type clauses stated there. Modern terminology of multiplicative type is a comparison label, not substituted ink.

The smoothness equivalences match final EGA IV4 Theorem17.5.1 (1967). The preceding typescript proof matches final Proposition17.4.9. Crucially, the draft fibrewise proposition labelled17.4.10 was not retained at that number: final17.4.10 is a remark about formally unramified morphisms locally of finite type. The draft proposition follows from final17.4.1(d), since the f-fibre over y equals the f_s-fibre. These final passages were read in the downloaded primary PDF; the numbering difference is recorded rather than silently equated.

scope_note: The graph-coordinate/Gaussian-elimination argument is independently verified in §10. Exact-title searches for the English fragment did not identify its author or publication; mathematical standardness is distinct from bibliographic identification. The arbitrary-dimensional or arbitrary-intermediate-field extension must retain the specified rational structures. Stacks089R Lemma27.22.1 verifies the finite-dimensional graph-coordinate charts; it is a modern mathematical comparator, not an attribution of the typescript.

The finite-basis coefficient argument is standard linear algebra and independently re-proved here. Exact searches for the fragment's title and its linear/multilinear wording gave no primary attribution. This is not assigned to Grothendieck merely because it survives among his sheets. Stacks089R Lemma27.22.1 verifies the finite-dimensional graph-coordinate charts; it is a modern mathematical comparator, not an attribution of the typescript.

The finite-etale theory of strictly henselian local schemes gives the trivial group; SGA1 XIII5.3.0 computes the normal-crossing complement by two Kummer directions. The possible omitted complement is a scan question, not an adopted correction.

Stacks04V8 describes root stacks with stabilizers along the divisor. For [A1_z/mu_n], t=z^n, stabilizers vanish off0; for Bmu_n×A1 they are present everywhere. This rejects an identification in commentary while retaining the useful finite-Kummer link.

Stacks03PK explicitly states the fppf and invertible-etale Kummer sequences. The algebra A[z]/(z^n−a), a a unit, is finite free faithfully flat; invertibility of nz^(n−1) gives etaleness when n is invertible. This does not extend etale Kummer theory to n=p in characteristicp.

Neron1965 III4.1 and the later exact comparison in Pepin2012 §1–2 concern the decomposition of the Neron pairing into intersection and component-group correction terms. Lang1957 gives related reciprocity. The precise source of this page101 and the definitions of j_o and the superscript-s cycles were not identified by exact-phrase, Numdam, author-bibliography and backward-citation searches. These are strong comparators, not a claimed textual identification.

The general geometric-irreducibility assertion is established. Poonen–Slavov Theorem1.8 and §7 prove that the bad hyperplanes are a finite exceptional-image union plus a constructible set of dimension≤codim(image)+1; when image dimension≥2 this is a proper subset of the dual projective space. This covers arbitrary morphisms of geometrically irreducible finite-type varieties, without properness or normality. Generic successive sections give the stated higher-codimension range. SGA1X2.10 invokes Bertini under its proper/normal hypotheses; the exact broader development is classified B rather than silently assigned to that narrower printed invocation. The paper traces the earlier theorem to Jouanolou1983 Theorem6.3(4), whose text was not opened here.

The opened EGA IV4 and SGA1 passages establish the local unramified/smooth machinery and the global irreducibility argument. Avoidance of a locus with image dimension<s is immediate for a generic codimension-s linear section. However, the exact combined unibranch/normal/smooth formulation has not been identified with one unchanged printed theorem; its local-property clauses and field-extension hypotheses remain separated. This is a partial precise match, not an assertion that every clause is still open.

SGA1 X1.8 verifies proper base-field invariance and X2.10–2.11 the section-surjectivity mechanism. X1.10 explicitly gives characteristic-p failures without properness. The page itself refuses to assert full nonproper base-changed surjectivity; the earlier notes should not erase this limitation.

SGA1 X2.10–2.11 proves the hyperplane version by generic Bertini and Zariski connectedness. For higher codimension, the reconstruction uses the universal Grassmannian incidence family, whose total space and geometric generic fibre are irreducible. Properness and Stein connectedness over the normal Grassmannian give geometrically connected special fibres. Applying this to connected finite étale covers requires the stated geometric-unibranch/local hypotheses. Merely iterating a special-hyperplane theorem would be insufficient because an intermediate special section need not be irreducible; no such iteration is used here.

SGA7 XVIII6.1 is the published tame-surjectivity argument using SGA1 XIII specialization. Esnault–Kindler2016 Theorem1.1 gives the regular strict-normal-crossing version under Lef, and an isomorphism under Leff plus intersection of all effective divisors. Their result and §6 handle stated variants, but do not silently identify every draft boundary convention.

The question is settled: Deligne WeilII4.2.7–4.2.8 proves the sufficiently general pencil result with Q_l coefficients; Orgogozo2005/2006 §11.2–11.4 proves conjugacy and equality of monodromy images for every Lefschetz pencil, without a transversality restriction, with Z/l^nu coefficients, l≠char(k). Illusie2006 Theorem5.2 states this explicitly and credits Gabber's image-equality argument to a letter of14March2005. Irreducibility follows with the usual vanishing-cohomology/Lefschetz assumptions; no such condition is dropped.

This is the stabilizer functoriality of SGA1 covering theory. The inserted separatedness hypothesis is exactly what makes agreement on a schematically dense open imply equality. The source itself distinguishes existence from uniqueness; the normalized-extension claim needs its finite/normal hypotheses.

SGA1 XIII Kummer descriptions and SGA7 I§1 supply the Tate-module inertia with cyclotomic action. Conjugacy of abstract subgroups alone is weaker; the source's Remords supplies the common coefficient trivialization. Distinct boundary components need not have identical inertia classes before the stated comparison.

The published Grothendieck–Serre correspondence dates this exact letter18August1959 and reproduces its conceptual hesitation. Nori's pointed group scheme over k and Zhang/Pauly base-extension results show that geometric base change is a real hypothesis, not automatic. A k-rational point and a geometric point are not interchangeable definitions.

SGA1 IX and SGA3 X6.1–6.3 develop this generators-and-relations description, including component and basepoint hypotheses. Bourbaki195 A§§2–3 gives the pro-object formalism. The specific boxed word relation is a choice-dependent presentation, not an invariant formula without the chosen paths.

This is Hilbert's Nullstellensatz: k-valued points already suffice, and every such point also defines a K-valued point. Conversely nilpotent images vanish in a field. The theorem is standard before these leaves; exact source authorship of the typescript is unidentified.

The uniform-completion construction predates these SGA leaves and is standard Bourbaki general topology. Searches for the exact wording have not identified the typescript edition/page. The ambient X/W symbols in the transcribed composition formula need scan inspection; the argument must concern the induced entourages on the completion.

SGA1 X1.3–1.7 supplies the homotopy exact sequence and the field product formula, with properness and geometric connectedness retained. The manuscript's diagram proof reduces the relative assertion to that sequence; no arbitrary nonproper Kunneth statement follows. Both parallel leaves149/151 were read.

SGA4 gives the classifying-topos formalism. The displayed H0=Hom(pi_s,E) cannot mean equivariant maps from the regular pi-set, which give E rather than E^pi; Hom from the one-point trivial object is the consistent formula. The cancellation does not refute the standard theorem.

SGA1 V1–4 and VIII give the finite-Galois-category and effective-descent framework. The fibrewise n! frame calculation proves the construction and the stabilizer quotient gives back X. A connected component of P yields a connected Galois cover when X is connected; P itself need not be connected.

The finite-etale case is standard SGA1 V quotient theory. On the line with doubled origin over A1, the involution swapping origins is identity on the common punctured line; its free locus consists of the origins and is not open. This meets etaleness and finite-group-action hypotheses, so the tentative finite-case correction is essential.

SGA1 V4.1–4.2 is the exact established Galois-category theorem. Each draft alternative must be compared with the full final axioms; the mere labels Gal1–6 do not certify equivalence. The source provides a route to the published framework, not a proved new axiom system.

SGA1 VIII/IX and Bourbaki190 give fpqc descent, while SGA3 X6.1 spells out effective-descent and connected-component assumptions. A non-surjective flat open immersion is not an epimorphic cover, so the possible missing faithfully is a substantive reading alarm. No blanket theorem for every draft D is assigned.

The proper Stein-factor/normalization and connected-fibre homotopy arguments in SGA1 IX–X give the finite-index statement. The word conoyau is interpreted as index, not a quotient group unless normality of the image is supplied. Properness and target normality are not optional, as the adjacent nodal example shows.

SGA1 X2.5 explicitly gives the full Zhat nodal graph example. Cyclically gluing n normalizations supplies finite etale cyclic covers for every n, including n=p. The source may have an omitted prime-to-p convention; the ink is not changed.

Gabber's constructibility theorem (as exposed by Deglise Theorem1.1) controls finite-set direct images for finite-type maps of noetherian schemes, but constructibility is weaker than local constancy or finite-etale representability. SGA1 IX descent and X proper separable cases are exact established special cases. The draft universal-open criterion was not matched to an opened theorem with all its quantifiers.

SGA3 X6.1–6.2 is the later framework for representable constant-group torsors. Equalizers of two pointed maps are clopen reductions; connectedness forces the reduction containing the chosen point to cover S. This is not the finite-flat S-group equalizer argument refuted in CL-SA12-223.

SGA3 X6.2 explicitly states strict prorepresentability for connected locally noetherian S; the corrected edition notes that one deduction can be expanded. For topological inverse limits, Bhatt–Scholze Lemma7.4.6 shows the same discrete torsor representations are recovered. The group-homomorphism statement must not be confused with the false arbitrary-Set criterion of scan183.

SGA3 X6 and Bhatt–Scholze §7 place discrete actions in their appropriate covering categories. The pro-etale Noohi group classifies a larger geometric-covering category; its profinite and prodiscrete completions recover different classical parts. This does not make every arbitrary admissible module on the page a finite etale local system.

Finite-etale descent and henselian invariance are established in SGA1 VIII/IX and are independent of a choice among compatible standard cover topologies. For infinite groups, SGA3 X6 explicitly assumes representable torsors and the corrected edition flags the passage from arbitrary fpqc torsor sheaves; the manuscript's whole C1–C5 comparison was not matched. It is not replaced by the finite theorem.

Artin–Mazur1967/1969 constructs etale homotopy and its comparison maps; Bourbaki195 and SGA4 supply prorepresentability machinery. The transcription identifies an H1 with a limit of H2 and changes indexing, so it cannot be cited as a precise theorem without choosing the intended cover and coefficients. The exact reconstructed low-degree sequence is conditional on H1-vanishing, not supplied by the title alone.

The effective-descent cocycle formalism is developed in SGA1 VIII/IX and SGA3 X6.1/6.3. That supplies established instances, while the particular diagram with unspecified fibration objects remains a programme. No universal nonabelian exact sequence is read into the fragment.

SGA3 X6.1–6.3 is an exact published match. Corrected-edition notes add openness of S′ components and connectedness, remove unnecessary openness of cube components, and explain the extra basepoint generators. The draft n″−n′ count is an upper-bound presentation under its normalization, not automatically an off-by-one error.

SGA3 X6.1 assumes universal effective descent for the category under consideration, and its corrected footnote47 distinguishes scheme torsors from arbitrary fpqc torsor sheaves. Bhatt–Scholze7.4.6 classifies etale torsors under discrete groups, but does not by itself settle all the manuscript's fpqc effectiveness claims. The unclear margin is a reading question, not proof of resolution.

SGA3 X6.3 expresses the relative group using the simplicial component object and its marked fibre; the corrected connected-cone condition is stronger evidence than a generic van Kampen analogy. The manuscript's explicit pi0=pi1=1 assumptions are retained.

The Baire example K_i=N^i meets all three displayed assumptions, but f(x)=x_(x0+1) is continuous without factoring through one finite prefix. Thus the proposed sufficiency criterion is false. Uniform continuity to a discrete target, or a finite compact inverse system, repairs this example. Bourbaki195 warns that an ordinary inverse limit does not replace a pro-object; Bhatt–Scholze7.4.6 concerns group homomorphisms, which are uniformly continuous, and does not contradict the counterexample.

This follows directly from the universal property of the colimit in topological spaces: a map out is continuous exactly when all component maps are. It does not show that every natural transformation of such restricted Set-valued functors comes from a continuous map, nor does it rescue the false criterion on scan183. Bourbaki195 supplies the variance distinction for representable functors.

SGA3 X6.3 gives the component-simplicial group construction; Artin–Mazur develops a broader etale homotopy type. Localic and pro-etale work are relevant later frameworks, but the manuscript does not specify a unique higher categorical theorem. Searches found no exact match for every proposed category-valued extension; no claim of undeveloped novelty is made.

The intended theorem follows from Nagata finite normalization and the normal-target birational form of Zariski's main theorem; the independent proof in §8 corrects the direction of the argument. The displayed normalization→X arrow already fails for a strict open immersion into normal Y. Stacks normalization/generically finite references verify the standard inputs; the faulty arrow is listed for scan review. Stacks37.43.2 (02LR) supplies the quasi-finite separated normalization factorization; apply it to quasi-compact local pieces before invoking the global finite-component argument, so quasi-compactness is not assumed at the step being proved.

This is the exact Corollary3.5 in SGA3VIII. A character is killed by n exactly when it factors through M/nM. Every group-algebra basis element has nth power1, giving integrality; finite generation gives finiteness. The finite example in torsion_grading_checks.json illustrates the universal argument, not a substitute for it.

SGA3VIII§4 is the exact published construction. Affineness descends fpqc from the affine structural group. Expanding a coaction in the group-algebra basis yields a direct M-grading, and the coaction counit/coassociativity give the grading identities. The strong-grading criterion is stated here as a reconstruction of the torsor condition, not as a quotation of the truncated paragraph.
